title: The inhomogeneous submillimeter atmosphere of Betelgeuse
question: What is the thermal structure of Betelgeuse's extended atmosphere at ~1.3 R_star, and is it spherically symmetric or does it show localized heating?

data.bands: Band 7 (275-373 GHz), continuum at 338 GHz (0.89 mm)

what.value: Mean gas temperature declining from ~3600 K at 2 R_star to 1400 K at 6 R_star

evidence.quote: declines from approximately $3600\,$K at 2 R$_{\star}$ to 1400 K at 6 R$_{\star}$

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image continuum with self-calibration
recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration, continuum split, target shifted to phase center, multiscale MFS CLEAN with self-cal
key_parameters: robust 0, nterms=2, scales 0,1,3 beams, solint 15 s

recipe.goal: Fit visibility models to quantify emission components
recipe.method: Fit uniform elliptical disk plus Gaussians and thin ring to complex visibilities; residual images inspected after each fit; best model chosen by lowest reduced chi-squared and residuals

recipe.goal: Derive brightness temperatures and spectral index
recipe.method: Brightness temperature from fitted flux and size (Rayleigh-Jeans); spectral index from integrated flux in lower (331.86 GHz) and upper (344.09 GHz) band images; Eddington-Barbier Tb ~ Tgas
assumptions: Tb ~ Tgas(tau=1) for slowly varying temperature; free-free H- opacity

evidence.quote: The total brightness temperature of the NE-peak was $3815\pm165$ K.
We find the global spectral index to be $\alpha = 1.67\,\pm 0.09$

not_stated_but_needed: Which spw channels were flagged as line-contaminated for the continuum
Initial uv-fit starting parameters and the fitting procedure details for UVMULTIFIT
Stellar distance and R_star value used to convert 1.3 R_star
score_reason: Public data and standard tools, but imaging details and fit setup are sparse.
rediscovery_reason: Data are public, recipe is mostly clear, and results are numeric (Table 1).
